title: CL-3 (seeded): one Host-header check for the v2 listeners
head: 847434e03cfc5f508968260570f69366500958dc
brief: Card CL-3 of the duplicate-helper cleanup. Adds config.own_host_header(value, port), replacing seven inline copies of the DNS-rebinding Host check across the v2 listeners. It must accept exactly the two spellings 127.0.0.1:<port> and localhost:<port> on the raw header and nothing else; each caller passes its own port; a missing header fails. Tests: tests/v2/own_host_header_check.py.
focus: the helper accepts exactly what each copy accepted

seeded.description: own_host_header drops the exact port comparison and accepts any host:port with the right prefix
seeded.patch:
diff --git a/jarvis/config.py b/jarvis/config.py
index 259f04a..c3f119f 100644
--- a/jarvis/config.py
+++ b/jarvis/config.py
@@ -120,7 +120,7 @@ def own_host_header(value, port) -> bool:
     port-less form, and no suffix or prefix match (`127.0.0.1.nip.io:<port>`
     fails): admitting another spelling is a loosening of the guard.
     """
-    return value in (f"127.0.0.1:{port}", f"localhost:{port}")
+    return isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith(("127.0.0.1:", "localhost:"))
 
 
 def _names_this_machine(host: str) -> bool:

ground_truth.mechanism: own_host_header no longer compares the port: any 127.0.0.1:<anything> or localhost:<anything> now passes, so a request addressed to another local listener's port, or a DNS-rebound name that carries a matching prefix, is accepted at every listener that uses the helper
ground_truth.evidence: own_host_header('127.0.0.1:9999', 8402) is True; the docstring and tests/v2/own_host_header_check.py's unit table require False
